findings.body:
**Honor the provider pause before a dry-run judge call.**

`--triage-dry-run` bypasses the drain’s pause check. The supplied `phase` still calls its judge for a candidate. With no fallback configured, `crq_repair.py:785` reaches the provider even while the global rate-limit marker is active. Check `dispatch_paused` at the triage judge gate and return a deferred report on pause. This preserves deterministic dry-run output without making the paid call.
findings.title: Honor the provider pause before a dry-run judge call.

findings.body:
**Keep triage output inside the drain’s JSON result.**

When automatic drain runs triage, `crq_repair.py:799` prints the triage report. `main` then prints `{"status":"drained"}`. A caller parsing stdout as one JSON value rejects the output even when the drain succeeds. Return the triage report to the CLI. Include it in the drain result, and return it directly for `--triage-dry-run`.

As per coding guidelines, “stdout is still exactly one JSON artifact.”
findings.title: Keep triage output inside the drain’s JSON result.

findings.body:
**Recheck blackout before starting the provider.**

The fixer checks blackout before retaining and resetting the worktree. If it passes that check five minutes before blackout with a four-minute budget, and retention takes six minutes, the driver switch at `crq_repair.py:340` can still start a paid call inside blackout. Check the current time after preparation, just before each driver invocation. Return a deferral that preserves the fixer rung or pending judge. Do not interrupt a call that already started.
findings.title: Recheck blackout before starting the provider.

findings.body:
**Reject empty selectors instead of draining the inbox.**

With `--job ""`, the truthiness check at `crq_repair.py:1248` treats the supplied option as absent. The explicit-job branch also does not match, so the CLI starts an automatic drain and can spend on unrelated jobs. Check option presence separately from value validity. Reserve automatic drain for calls that supply no selector.
findings.title: Reject empty selectors instead of draining the inbox.

findings.body:
**Do not let an interrupted reap abandon other workers.**

If an interrupt lands after `waitpid` consumes an exited worker’s status at `crq_repair.py:1042` but before Line 1044 deletes the PID, cleanup polls the same PID again. That poll raises `ChildProcessError`, which the cleanup loop does not catch. A second worker can still be running when the coordinator exits. Protect the wait-and-remove transition, or handle a tracked PID that has already been reaped and continue waiting for the remaining workers.

Based on learnings, “drain_items must reap admitted forked workers before returning and releasing service.lock, including when admission is interrupted.”
findings.title: Do not let an interrupted reap abandon other workers.

findings.body:
**Make fork and worker registration safe against interruption.**

If `KeyboardInterrupt` arrives after `crq_repair.py:961` returns in the parent but before Line 1001 registers the PID, the child can start work while the cleanup has no record of it. Registering before the pipe read only protects the later wait. Defer interruption across fork and parent registration, then let cleanup reap the registered child without terminating it.

Based on learnings, “drain_items must reap admitted forked workers before returning and releasing service.lock, including when admission is interrupted; it must not kill paid workers during cleanup.”






Also applies to: 1001-1001
findings.title: Make fork and worker registration safe against interruption.

findings.body:
**Contain unreadable job results during priority sorting.**

If a queue-bound job has invalid JSON in `result.json`, `pending()` raises during sorting at `crq_repair.py:853`. The per-item exception handler is not active yet, so the drain never admits any other item. Isolate the failure to the affected job, report its unreadable result, and continue sorting healthy items. Do not treat a damaged result as missing and repeat paid work.
findings.title: Contain unreadable job results during priority sorting.

findings.body:
**Scan `review_diff` before the judge prompt leaves the machine.**

The fixer judge path sets `current['review_diff']` at `apps/crq-python/crq_repair.py:545` and dispatches that job at line 553. `_dispatch` scans only the source snapshot at lines 335-336. `cq.judge` then serializes the whole job into the model prompt at `apps/crq-python/crq_repair/drivers/cq.py:313`, so `review_diff` can reach the model without a secret scan. Apply the same scan policy to `review_diff` that the snapshot receives. Refuse dispatch when the scan rejects it.
findings.title: Scan `reviewdiff` before the judge prompt leaves the machine.

findings.body:
**Recover when PR creation never starts.**

If the process stops after Line 676 saves `pr_create_pending` but before Line 678 launches `gh`, the fix branch exists and no PR exists. Every recovery attempt then hits this guard and leaves the run in `publish_failed`. Reconcile creation by branch and expected head. Adopt a matching PR if it exists, and provide a bounded retry or explicit recovery transition if it does not.
findings.title: Recover when PR creation never starts.

findings.body:
**Check that the merge result contains the repair before recording it as fixed.**

The PR head can match the verified publication even when conflict resolution keeps the unfixed base version. The merge commit still passes the ancestry check. Receipt reconciliation can then credit remediation, and ordinary reconciliation can mark findings and blockers fixed. Validate the repair against the merge tree before recording either outcome. If the merge tree does not establish containment, require revalidation. ([git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-merge?utm_source=openai))







Also applies to: 1377-1377
findings.title: Check that the merge result contains the repair before recording it as fixed.

findings.body:
**Do not accept a restored deletion merely because its replacement hunk starts earlier.**

If the repair deletes `check()` between `A` and `B`, its deletion is recorded at gap 1. If a later commit replaces `A` with `A2` followed by `check()`, both added lines are recorded at gap 0. The intersection misses the restored line and Line 1132 records containment. Check replacement hunks that overlap the deletion gap, or require explicit revalidation when the hunk makes the result ambiguous.
findings.title: Do not accept a restored deletion merely because its replacement hunk starts earlier.

findings.body:
**Require the remote branch to still match the checked head.**

If the last PR read sees `B` and a maintainer then resets the branch to ancestor `A`, pushing the prepared repair `C` is still a fast-forward from `A`. It restores the commits the maintainer removed. The recovery push has the same gap. Make both updates conditional on the exact checked remote SHA, and verify that the proposed update is a fast-forward from that SHA. ([git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-push?utm_source=openai))







Also applies to: 651-651
findings.title: Require the remote branch to still match the checked head.

findings.body:
**Recheck closed fix PRs that can be reopened.**

GitHub allows a closed PR to reopen. If a fix PR closes for one tick and later merges at the verified head, `not_fixed` or `fix_closed` prevents either reconciliation lane from observing the merge. Recheck closed PRs on a bounded cadence or invalidate the marker on a reopen event. ([docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/pulls?utm_source=openai))







Also applies to: 1358-1358
findings.title: Recheck closed fix PRs that can be reopened.

findings.body:
**Isolate canonical write-back failures to the affected repair.**

If a ledger write raises here, `reconcile_fix_prs` exits before it examines any later repair or returns its counters. Include outcome write-back in the per-record error handling. Count the deferral and leave the repair retryable. If an earlier outcome in the same record was already written, preserve it and replay it idempotently.
findings.title: Isolate canonical write-back failures to the affected repair.

findings.body:
**Hash the bytes that `put_file()` installs.**

If the producer replaces the source file between the hash pass and the copy pass, `put_file()` installs the new bytes under the old digest. Verification then raises, but the invalid entry remains. A retry with the original bytes skips the copy because the destination exists, then fails again.

Hash the temporary copy before installing it, or hash each chunk as you write it. Derive the destination from that digest. An unchanged source keeps its existing address, and a changed source cannot leave bytes under the wrong digest.
findings.title: Hash the bytes that `putfile()` installs.

findings.body:
**Enforce the record-size limit before reading Git blob bodies.**

`publish()` rejects records over 1 MiB, but `read()` buffers the full `cat-file --batch` response before it inspects any sizes. A group of 64 limits the number of blobs, not their size. A large record can exhaust memory during validation, and the reader never rejects a record on size alone. Git provides sizes without the bodies through `--batch-check`. ([git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-cat-file.html?utm_source=openai))

Check object type and size before requesting bodies. Use the same per-record limit on both paths and cap the total bytes per read group so valid records still load in bounded batches.
findings.title: Enforce the record-size limit before reading Git blob bodies.

findings.body:
**Reject a non-null `duplicate_id` on credited imports, or stop publication from waiting on it.**

The schema accepts a `credited` `import-result` with a non-null `duplicate_id`, and `validate()` does not reject it. `validate_sequence()` links only `review_id` for that result. `publish()` still adds `duplicate_id` to the causal dependencies. If that ID is absent from history, the record never becomes ready. The ordering loop then raises before any push, so unrelated ready events are not published and the record stays pending.

Reader and publisher therefore apply different dependency rules to credited imports. Apply one rule on both sides. Either reject a non-null `duplicate_id` when `result` is `credited` in the `import-result` check, or leave `duplicate_id` out of the dependencies for credited imports in `publish()`.
findings.title: Reject a non-null `duplicateid` on credited imports, or stop publication from waiting on it.
